speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These include residential, commercial, institutional and utility uses, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It is important that state land is protected from unauthorised use and damage, as such acts can impede Singapore's development, create public safety issues and affect public enjoyment of our scarce resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: However, there have been individuals in the past who encroached significantly on state land and refused to remove their encroachments, even after the impact of their actions was explained to them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: One such case, which was reported in the news some time back, involves private landowners who extended their property on to adjoining state land by building structures on it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This act disrupted and delayed PUB's drainage improvement works in the area.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The landowners refused to remove the encroachments, despite extensive engagement and multiple deadline extensions granted by the authorities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Singapore Land Authority (SLA) eventually filed charges against the landowners for trespassing on state land under the State Lands Encroachment Act 1883 (SLEA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The SLEA, which contains the current enforcement framework, will be repealed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Outdated provisions, such as the appointment of forest rangers and penghulus to carry out duties, which are no longer relevant to modern Singapore, will also be removed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: I will now take the House through the key features of this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Part 1 of the Bill introduces the fundamental concepts used in the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill defines state land to include lands that are unalienated, vested, surrendered or acquired by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill does not deal exhaustively with all state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Excluded are unalienated lands managed by PUB, NParks and LTA under their respective legislation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is to avoid the overlapping of laws and criminalising of activities on state lands that are already under the management of these public sector agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill also includes updated definitions to better reflect and capture present-day activities which constitute unauthorised use of state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill clarifies the definition of a "structure" which, when erected on, under or over state land, may constitute an encroachment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This includes land reclamation works and external features which protrude outwards from buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Part 2 also sets out the proceedings in Court that may be taken to recover state land from improper use and unauthorised activities on state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A non-exhaustive list of unauthorised activities deemed to be offences under the Bill includes unauthorised clearance and digging of state land; unauthorised enclosure of state land; unauthorised dumping and leaving of waste on state land; and unauthorised works for the reclamation of land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Under the new Bill, the penalties have been raised to align with penalties for comparable offences in newer legislation, such as the Parks and Trees Act and the Environmental Public Health Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These present penalties in section 7 of SLEA are no longer deterrent vis-a-vis a fine not exceeding $5,000, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or both.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In the case of a continuing offence, a further fine of up to $500 will be imposed for each day during which the offence continues after conviction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Higher penalties may be imposed for a repeat offence of disposing rubbish or waste on state land using a vehicle.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, a new provision in the Bill now provides that the Court may order a convicted offender to compensate the Government for the costs and expenses incurred by an electricity or gas licensee or the PUB in complying with a Court order to discontinue the supply of electricity, gas or water.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill thus provides for a wider scope of compensation than what is available under the current SLEA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This includes situations where there is irreparable damage or harm caused to state land, or where state land may collapse, or cause the collapse of adjacent land, or pose a danger to the public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Today, under current law, SLA must serve a notice giving 28 days for the unlawful occupants to vacate the state land and remove their movable property.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If they do not vacate and remove their movable property by the notice timeframe, SLA must obtain a warrant for dispossession from the Court to remove unlawful occupants on state land and seize and forfeit any movable property.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: SLA must also obtain a Court order for the demolition of unlawful buildings and structures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Under the existing process, the time taken for the removal of encroachments can be lengthy, during which the offender can continue his or her offence on the state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, the existing process does not allow for much flexibility to adopt a differentiated approach taking into consideration the complexity and seriousness of each case.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Specifically, the Bill enables an authorised officer to serve an encroachment notice to any person whom the officer has reasonable cause to believe is engaged in the improper use of state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The encroachment notice will require the person to abate the encroachment by a specified date.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It will also include an objection period, during which the person can give an objection if he or she does not wish to comply with the notice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If there is non-compliance with the notice and no objection is received, the authorised officer can proceed to seize and remove any movable property involved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If an objection is received, the authorised officer may then file a complaint to the Magistrate's Court on the unauthorised activity committed on the state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Part 4 of the Bill sets out the circumstances under which abandoned private land may be resumed to become state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The current SLEA already sets out the mechanism by which alienated land, which has been abandoned for three years or more, may be forfeited to the state.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill retains this three-year threshold but makes some changes to update the resumption process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The process begins when the Minister for Law grants approval for a particular piece of land to be declared liable for forfeiture to the state.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Following this, a notice of the declaration must be made in the Government Gazette.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is similar to the current process under SLEA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: However, under the Bill, there will no longer be a requirement for a physical notice of the declaration to be posted on the land in the English, Malay, Chinese and Tamil languages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Instead, SLA will publish the notice in the four official languages in the major local newspapers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This ensures that there will still be adequate publicity of the fact.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Otherwise, the land will be deemed forfeited to the state.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Part 5 of the Bill provides for the various powers of enforcement that can be exercised in the administration of the Bill, provided that the relevant statutory thresholds are met.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: To aid investigation, the Bill empowers authorised officers to: (a) Enter either state land, or any other land, in or from which the officer has reasonable grounds to suspect an offence under the Bill may be committed, and inspect, make documentation of, and take extracts from the land or anything on that land; (b) Request documents and information from any person reasonably believed to be acquainted with the circumstances relevant to the suspected commission of an offence under the Bill; and (c) Request an individual found in, on or near any state land to disclose his or her identity and place of residence if the officer has reasonable grounds to suspect that the individual has committed or is attempting to commit an offence under this Bill in relation to that state land.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As in many other laws, the obstruction of an authorised officer in the discharge of his or her duties under this Bill, as well as the intentional tampering with any encroachment notice or summons, will be offences under the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Part 6 of the Bill provides for the appointment of officers for the administration of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In particular, SLA may appoint enforcement officers from among public officers, employees of any public authority except a Town Council and any auxiliary police officer appointed under the Police Force Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The enforcement officer's role is to assist SLA in the administration of the Bill in any particular area in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This is necessary as land is one of our most valuable resources for the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These changes will allow SLA and the agencies overseeing the management of state land to take effective measures to protect our state land from damage and misuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, on behalf of the Minister for Law, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: State land belongs to all Singaporeans and we must protect it from being damaged or unfairly used for private purposes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I, thus, support this much needed review of the law, but I have three clarifications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification relates to the defence against an offence of unauthorised use of state land.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In some cases, it is fairly obvious that the land is state land, such as setting up makeshift structures or farms in forest areas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But it is less clear in cases involving the boundaries of private property and state land.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The average home owner would not know whether their fence crosses into state land.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Home owners would likely rely on the expertise of their contractors to ensure compliance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Workmen would also rely on the instructions of their managers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would reliance on the due diligence of third parties be enough to make up the defence in section 7?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to the OneMap app example in the explanatory statement, can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary give guidance when someone would not be reasonably expected to know if the land was state land?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification relates to the process for objecting to an encroachment notice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that encroachment might involve a person's home and that rectification might be complex or expensive, there must be sufficient time to seek advice on whether to raise objections to the encroachment notice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary confirm that reasonable time will be given to raise objections, proportionate to the facts of each case?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, where objections are raised, the Act is silent on any procedure for the authority to consider the objection and notify the recipient of the results or reasons for rejecting the objection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Instead, it only states that on receiving an objection, the officer may make a criminal complaint to a magistrate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This approach appears to skip the necessary steps to resolve the objection in a clear and transparent manner.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that land issues can be sensitive due to costs or attachments formed, we should have a clear process to reach a smooth resolution.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify if, prior to a criminal complaint, the authority will notify the result of the objection and give time to comply with the encroachment notice?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My final clarification relates to the forfeiture of abandoned land.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given the scarcity of land in Singapore, it would be economically efficient to ensure that abandoned land is reclaimed by the state and applied to the benefit of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the authority be taking active steps to identify abandoned land and use these processes to recover land as state land, and then reinject it into the market?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The last review was 48 years ago, almost half a century ago.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I wish to seek clarifications in three areas.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we should leverage the use of technology for the reporting and verification of state land issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should count on them to report issues that were missed during routine inspections.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We have the OneService app that allows for easy, one-stop reporting of municipal issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Even when issues are reported to the wrong category, they are rerouted to the correct agency to be worked on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Most importantly, this ensures that the resident need not approach different agencies to get their issues settled.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, it may not be straightforward to give feedback pertaining to state land.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There is comparatively less awareness about accessible and reliable information resources.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In fact, unknown to most, the OneMap app and website provide extensive information about land ownership in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clicking on the land lots on the digital map displays the responsible agencies and contact information.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Does SLA intend to promote its use amongst the public?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can residents, in fact, use the OneService app to report or seek clarification on state land encroachment cases?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Is there a one-stop public hotline for residents who are less tech-savvy?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When there is less ambiguity and a simplified reporting process, problems can be quickly identified and resolved.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: OneMap is a comprehensive resource on land ownership in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, what is on a digital map may differ from actual ground.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Unlike a map, there are no clear boundary markers on the ground.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Misunderstandings or unintentional encroachment may arise when the resident property and state property are bordering each other and if the boundary is unclear.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: At present, the onus is on the individual to prove that, only on a balance of probabilities, he did not know and could not have reasonably been expected to know, that the land concerned was state land.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry clarify how can the individual prove this?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How does one prove that they do not have the knowledge?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How do the authorities differentiate between ignorance and negligence in checking?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can we do away with this concept in the first place?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, when multiple Government agencies have a stake in managing a piece of state land, ambiguity must be kept minimal.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For example, the greenery on a piece of state land is centrally maintained by NParks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Cleaning comes under the Department of Public Cleanliness in NEA.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Despite the clear distinction, these issues are often intertwined.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When there is illegal dumping on a piece of state land, NParks' maintenance work could be hindered before the problem is resolved.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This could manifest in other problems that inconvenience the residents living nearby.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Examples include pooling of water that leads to mosquito breeding or pest issues.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Which agency is, ultimately, responsible for resolving the issue at hand?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Is there a system in place to designate the responsible stakeholder, with the aim of resolving the problem as soon as possible?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some recent policies and initiatives may contribute to the complexity of enforcement.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For example, there is the Community in Bloom project under NParks, where residents can plant greenery in common spaces.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This may lead to the assumption or misunderstanding that residents can do more with the land outside their property and contrary to the intent of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Residents may use such land to create composts or do micro-farming, in the name of sustainability.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is usually innocuous and with good intentions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How do we strike a balance between giving residents discretion and a stake in improving their living environment, while preventing encroachment on state land?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Land encroachment becomes a potentially sensitive problem when religious artifacts or buildings are involved.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In fact, it is not rare to see religious paraphernalia, such as altars and statues, left at the foot of trees or on an empty plot of land.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I wonder if agencies have made exceptions for such cases because of their religious nature.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, laws should be applied fairly and consistently.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is the protocol for agencies to deal with encroachment when the offence is one of a sensitive nature?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can they count on guidance and support from religious organisations to do so when it is necessary?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I make reference to the discovery of skeletal remains of two sisters in an abandoned house in Upper Thomson.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: During this period, the first set of skeletal remains was detected in 2006 after NEA officers entered for a mosquito check.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The second set of remains was then found in 2015 by BCA contractors who were there to erect a temporary roof.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: From this example, it appears that it took a long time before any intervention was done.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Located on prime land, it received conservation status in 2008.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, it is largely derelict, though it is supposedly own by Lee Tat Development.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Is it just when there is no claim or when there is also a lack of development?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In line with the Upper Thomson example, abandoned land may prove an opportunity for criminals seeking to dispose of evidence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The new laws highlight the severity of misuse and encroachment of state land.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They reflect the Government's resolve to use our land prudently.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: More importantly, we need to put our residents at the heart of what we do.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I take a personal interest in this Bill because there is state land in my constituency.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: State lands do not just concern the state, or the Government, so to speak.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clarity is critical for the quick resolution of problems pertaining to state land.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Residents will often find themselves being in close proximity to state lands.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have some clarifications as well as suggestions on how the Bill can be expanded in the future.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I understand that this enhances SLA's operational efficiency, I have two questions.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, how does SLA work with other agencies, such as NEA, if there are concerns by neighbours of any threats on the abandoned land, for example, dengue or other public safety concerns, during this notice period?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, as the effect of shortening the notice is significant, I am concerned that three months may be too short as landowners may have legitimate reasons for being uncontactable – for instance, if they have migrated overseas.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I note that the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned publication in major newspapers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What efforts will SLA make to ascertain that landowners have received the notice by the end of the three months, if possible?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there have been cases in the past of the elderly, for example, who encroach on state land by secretly growing vegetables, having small religious altars or even sleeping rough in patches of forest.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could SLA provide an anonymised breakdown of the profile of individuals who commit these offences?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This could help us to really understand if the increased penalties are, in fact, proportional as a deterrent.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In other cases, residents of private landed estates may, inadvertently, encroach on state land by expanding gardens, walkways, or even part of their homes, into small areas in between houses.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While land grabbing should certainly not be encouraged or excused, these residents do sometimes face challenges when coordinating with the authorities about the management of this public space.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For instance, state land might not be maintained for a long period of time, turning them into breeding grounds for mosquitoes.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In such situations, residents may take over the land and take care of it as they perceive it to be abandoned.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In such instances, the Bill should be supplemented by greater coordination efforts between SLA and home owners to encourage communication on land management concerns and ensure the timely management of state-owned spaces.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, it would be helpful, in particular, in landed estates, if there could be a more systematic and efficient way in vesting state land into the care of a particular agency for building and maintenance – for example, where such lands have formed useful but informal shortcuts for residents over time to access amenities, such as bus stops, outside of their estates.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some may hope to make such shortcuts safer and official with pavements and light fixtures.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, the considerations, timelines and processes for doing so are unclear.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Lastly, the Bill also allows enforcement officers to enter and inspect any land without a warrant if they have reasonable suspicion that the land is being used illegally.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They can then issue notices to the offenders to leave the land or fine the offenders.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Since no warrants or criminal proceedings are required for these actions, what measures will SLA take to prevent trespassing or scams under the pretext of a legitimate inspection?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, even as we protect what the eyes cannot see, we must not forget to protect what is harder to see but is also under threat – our sea spaces.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore needs to establish stronger regulations on land under water as well – our seabeds – to allow remaining marine life to flourish.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I sincerely hope that just because we are occasionally able to sight beautiful creatures in our waters, including blacktip reef sharks, dugongs, or even turtles and anemone fish, we should not take such things for granted and accept the status quo.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must be more proactive in protecting such gems.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore, currently, has one marine park set up in 2014 – that is, the Sisters' Islands.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Here, it is an offence to fish, collect coral, or moor boats, without NParks' permission.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, this marine park accounts for just 0.04% of Singapore's marine area.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: SLA manages the islands near Sisters' Islands, namely Saint John's, Lazarus and Kusu.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are multiple users of the waters around these islands, including recreation and research, to name a few.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Commercial fish farming also exists in the waters off these islands, which have an impact on the seabed, water and shores.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During COVID-19, visitor volume to these islands increased by 60%.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is good that more Singaporeans are appreciating our natural environment.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But increased carrying capacity comes with increasing impact and strain on the lands.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given the rising interest, I would like to ask what SLA envisions with regard to the protection and enhancement of these Southern Islands and their heritage.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Southern Islands' management, currently, straddles several Government bodies – NParks, SFA, SLA, URA and MPA, to name a few.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Perhaps the next step towards protecting state lands would be to have a more coordinated whole-of-Government approach to protect land on these islands and the surrounding waters to engage stakeholders with a more systematic framework and build institutional knowledge.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked whether the increased maximum fine for offences under clause 5 is a useful and proportional deterrent.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In particular, she cited cases involving individuals who are sleeping rough on state land, or retired seniors who engage in unauthorised cultivation on state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The enforcement framework set out in this Bill covers all manner of encroachment offences, taking into account the different circumstances of trespass.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Not all cases are, eventually, prosecuted in Court.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Also, in practice, SLA, generally, does engage and will continue to engage those encroaching on state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There would be an opportunity to rectify the encroachments first, absent irreparable damage or danger due to the encroachment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In cases involving rough sleepers on state land, SLA works very closely with MSF who will engage and provide support to these individuals.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This could include referring them to suitable shelters or accommodation, in the interest of their safety and well-being.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With regard to cases where enforcement action is taken, Mr Louis Ng asked about the defences available to those prosecuted under the Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This includes whether reliance on the due diligence of third parties would constitute a defence under clause 7 of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked, in relation to the same clause, how individuals who encroach on state land can prove that they did not know and could not have reasonably been expected to know, that the land concerned was state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The scenarios under which a defence may be constituted are varied and will depend on the particular circumstances of the case.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Nonetheless, the Members' underlying concern appears to be situations where an individual does not know that they are encroaching on state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The elements of the offence in this clause are engaging in the listed activities on state land without lawful authority and intentionally.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Also, as I mentioned earlier, SLA, typically, engages those encroaching on state land, before taking enforcement action.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the specific example raised by the two Members on private home owners, the property owner should also take responsibility to ensure that there is no encroachment onto adjoining state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This includes engaging a registered surveyor to carry out surveys to confirm if there are encroachments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If encroachments are found from the surveys, owners should check with SLA on whether the encroachment must be removed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: SLA will also be embarking on public education efforts after the Bill is passed, to raise public awareness of the new Bill and also address any misconceptions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Moving on to the process for abating encroachments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the timeline to comply with or raise objections to the encroachment notice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Ng also asked if the Authority would notify the result of the objection and provide time for individuals to comply with the notice before Court proceedings are initiated.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To provide some context, this draws on SLA's experience with past encroachment cases, where members of the public had requested that SLA take action against the reported encroachments quickly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is often because the encroachments might have posed disamenities and obstruction to the public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In addition, there might be cases where SLA needs to take action more quickly, for example, where there is ongoing harm being done to the state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Nevertheless, SLA will strike a balance between giving individuals time to rectify their encroachments and stopping the harm done by these encroachments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In general, SLA will provide a reasonable timeframe for owners to comply with encroachment notices, taking into consideration the nature and scale of the encroachments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On whether the Authority will notify potential offenders of the results of the objection, I would like to, first, clarify that once an objection is filed, clause 16 of the Bill allows the Authority to refer the matter to the Courts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The usual Court processes, after making a complaint to a Magistrate under the Criminal Procedure Code, will then apply.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That said, generally, SLA will respond to the potential offender on SLA's position on the basis of his or her objection, before filing a complaint to the Court.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Alternatively, the encroachment notice may be cancelled if there is merit in the case contained in the objection.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Apart from the process for objection, the Member's concern may also relate more broadly to whether there is sufficient notice given before matters are escalated to the point of legal action.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I have mentioned earlier, SLA, typically, engages those encroaching on state land before commencing any enforcement action.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, if there is a need to issue an encroachment notice, reasonable time will also be given to comply with the notice or to raise objections.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This will be proportionate to the facts of each case.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about encroachments involving religious artefacts or buildings.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First and foremost, the setting up of any structures or the leaving of any objects on state land without lawful authority would constitute an encroachment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That being said, similar to the approach for other types of encroachments, agencies, typically, engage owners of any religious items placed on state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Agencies will explain that these are unauthorised encroachments, before taking enforcement action, if needed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Where appropriate, SLA also works with the relevant religious organisations to ensure that the matter is handled sensitively and with respect.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about safeguards to prevent trespassing under the pretext of a legitimate inspection under the Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Authorised officers and enforcement officers must declare their office and produce their identification card when asked.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The owner of the private land can demand to see their credentials and when the officers seek entry for inspection or other purposes provided for in the Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These provisions are directed at preventing illegal trespassing and scams, such as what Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin had described.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the issue of public awareness and feedback, I thank Mr Yip Hong Weng for his suggestion to leverage the use of technology in interfacing with the public on state land issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, OneMap is an example of our multi-agency effort to provide reliable, timely and accurate location-based information and services to the public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: While SLA does not have data specifically on how often the public uses information from OneMap to provide feedback on state land, SLA does track the usage of OneMap.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: SLA regularly promotes OneMap through various social media channels.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It has also broadened its efforts to raise awareness of the services on OneMap to industry and members of the public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For example, SLA has signed collaborative Memoranda of Understanding with industry players, such as real estate agencies, developers and business chambers, to promote the use of geospatial solutions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: SLA will continue to review ways to raise awareness of OneMap.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin also raised important considerations about coordination between agencies and adopting a resident-centric approach in resolving land-related issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: When the maintenance of land straddles the purview of multiple agencies, we will ensure that agencies coordinate our responses such that the issues relating to state land are resolved promptly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We recognise that it can sometimes be confusing for members of the public to identify the agency-in-charge.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have taken efforts to streamline our touchpoints with the public and to address their feedback effectively and efficiently.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For instance, members of public can report or clarify state land issues using the OneService app, which is a one-stop platform where residents can provide feedback on municipal issues, without having to figure out which Government agency to contact.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: SLA will then follow up on any feedback or clarifications relating to state land issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In addition, members of the public can also contact SLA’s hotline to report any unauthorised use of state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: SLA will assist to direct feedback to the relevant agency if it is not within SLA’s purview.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To address Mr Louis Ng and Mr Yip Hon Weng’s questions, in general, we do not actively identify abandoned land to pursue resumption.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We, typically, take action when alerted to pieces of abandoned land that could pose a hazard to public safety or health.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This could arise from public feedback on maintenance and safety issues, as pointed out by Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin also highlighted situations where there are pressing concerns, such as dengue, which might require a quicker response.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In such cases, SLA will coordinate with the relevant agencies to consider the options available to address these concerns, even before the forfeiture process is completed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The cases of abandoned land that we have encountered thus far involve mainly isolated strips of land like back or side lanes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On Mr Yip Hon Weng’s query on the type of land that qualifies for forfeiture under the Bill, land is deemed to be abandoned and forfeited when no claims are established to it within the stipulated claim period.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In other words, the lack of development of a piece of land does not, in itself, allow the state to forfeit the land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Also, for cases involving land owned by deceased individuals without beneficiaries, such as the Upper Thomson Road case cited by the Member, the Government becomes entitled to the land, pursuant to the Intestate Succession Act 1967.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Public Trustee's Office has separate existing procedures to dispose of the land that has so accrued to the Government, in accordance with the Civil Law Act 1909 and the Probate and Administration Act 1934.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin’s question on the resumption notice, as mentioned in my speech earlier, a declaration will be made in the Government Gazette.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is similar to the current process under the State Lands Encroachments Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In addition, as mentioned in my opening speech, SLA will also now publish the notice in the four official languages in major local newspapers, including the digital versions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This improves upon the current process, where SLA affixes the physical notice on the land, as greater publicity can be secured through publishing the notice in the local media.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This includes cases where the potential claimants are not physically in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Taking this into consideration, potential claimants should have sufficient time within which they can claim compensation for their interest in the land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how we will strike a balance between protecting state land from unauthorised use and facilitating community use of state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As Members would be well aware, Singapore has limited land resources.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As custodian of our state land and properties, SLA is also continually looking for innovative ways in which our state land can be used to benefit the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Where there are suitable vacant state lands which are not required for immediate development, SLA will also work with other agencies to put out these sites for public recreational activities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The current list of these Community Use Sites can be found on SLA’s website.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Member has also mentioned NParks’ Community in Bloom initiative.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We encourage members of the public to take advantage of these initiatives.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Our concern with unauthorised cultivation and plantings on state land is that these can create potential health hazards, such as mosquito breeding hotspots, and impede the maintenance of state land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Unauthorised use of state land for activities can also affect public safety and, potentially, damage the land.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Separately, there were a number of comments relating to matters outside the ambit of this Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, I thank Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin for her suggestion on the vesting of land to facilitate maintenance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin may wish to file a separate Parliamentary Question on this matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will help provide her feedback to the relevant agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin also spoke about increasing protection for Singapore’s marine spaces, in particular, for the Southern Islands.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: While the question of marine spaces is not within the scope of this Bill, I agree that this is an important issue which should be further studied and we will convey her feedback to the relevant agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: SLA will also consider her suggestions in its management of the Southern Islands.
